cards.question: Which cricoid landmark identifies the level of cricoid pressure?
cards.answer: The cricoid cartilage is the only complete tracheal ring, lying anteriorly at C6. Palpate below the thyroid prominence to the first firm transverse band. Backward pressure of ~30 N (10 N awake, 30 N anaesthetised) occludes the oesophagus against the C6 vertebral body — though clinical effectiveness is debated.

cards.question: What is the sensory innervation of the larynx?
cards.answer: Above the cords: internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (vagus). Below the cords and trachea: recurrent laryngeal nerve. All intrinsic laryngeal muscles are supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve EXCEPT cricothyroid (external branch of superior laryngeal nerve). Bilateral RLN injury leaves cords in mid-position — stridor and airway emergency.

cards.question: Where is the cricothyroid membrane and how is it located?
cards.answer: Between the lower thyroid cartilage and upper cricoid, 1–2 cm below the laryngeal prominence in the midline. The "laryngeal handshake" — stabilising the larynx between thumb and middle finger while palpating downward with the index finger — reliably identifies it for emergency front-of-neck access.
